candidate: Harness-decided keep gate from repeated runs (A/A noise floor plus fixed seed panel)
what: The harness repeats the unchanged baseline, records the spread, and keeps a candidate only when its repeated-run mean beats the baseline by a margin declared before the loop and larger than that spread.
problem_here: Keeps must beat run-to-run noise and come from measurements the agent cannot influence.
mechanism: Harness launches baseline and candidate repeats with harness-assigned seeds and compares means; the agent only proposes.
evidence: pi-autoresearch v1.9.0 README: its confidence score is 'Advisory only -- never auto-discards' and uses the MAD of all metric values in a session; Hernandez blog (2026-04-10) measured cross-seed variance of about 0.005 val_bpb yet kept single runs; Google tuning playbook: 'consider running the best trial N times to characterize the run-to-run trial variance'.
cost: About five baseline runs per campaign plus k runs per candidate.
simpler_alternative: Single-run comparison with the best value, as upstream autoresearch does.
reason: Both reports ask for it and their own sources show the community tools do not enforce it. Agrees with the loop-autoresearch and search-hpo scouts.
cheap_local_trial: Run the bundled small task five times unchanged, record the spread, then pass a known-null and a known-good change through the gate.
checked: pi-autoresearch README and index.ts v1.9.0; google-research/tuning_playbook README; hectorhernandez.dev post; 2026-11-11

candidate: Bootstrap P(better) keep gate (pattern of rigor.py in trevin-creator/autoresearch-mlx)
what: Run candidate and best k times each, bootstrap P(mean(candidate) < mean(best)), keep when P >= 0.95; discard early when the first run is already worse than the best mean.
problem_here: A statistical keep rule that fits in the stdlib core.
mechanism: statistics and random only; 20,000 resamples with a fixed RNG seed; ledger rigor_ledger.jsonl with hash, desc, samples, mean, std, status, p_better; skips configurations already scored.
evidence: rigor.py read (repository MIT, 1,891 stars, last push 2026-07-02): --seeds default 3, --confidence default 0.95. Limit in the code: the seed is never varied, so repeats measure nondeterminism only. Scout inference: with 3 versus 3 runs P >= 0.95 needs near-complete separation.
maturity: One community script; no tests seen.
cost: k times the run cost per candidate.
simpler_alternative: Mean difference against a declared margin (row above).
reason: Shows the gate needs no package; false-keep rate and power at k=3 are untested and seeds must be varied.
cheap_local_trial: Replay recorded metric samples from the bundled task (A/A pairs and one real improvement) through the gate offline; count false keeps and misses.

candidate: Raw-MAD confidence ratio used as the keep gate (as the Gemini report describes pi-autoresearch)
what: Confidence = |best improvement| / MAD of the session's metric values; lock in at 2.0x, re-test below 1.0x.
problem_here: Proposed in a report as the keep rule of the kit.
mechanism: computeConfidence returns delta / mad; null with fewer than 3 points or MAD 0; no 1.4826 scale factor.
evidence: Contradicted as a gate: README says 'Advisory only -- never auto-discards ... the final keep/discard decision stays with the agent'; the MAD covers all experiments of a segment, not baseline repeats. Scout inference: for Gaussian noise raw MAD is about 0.6745 sigma, so 2.0x is about 1.35 sigma.
maturity: Released feature of a pi extension (MIT, 8,230 stars).
simpler_alternative: Keep gate from baseline repeats (first row).
reason: Mixes treatment effects with noise, is unscaled and is advisory in its own source. A scaled MAD over baseline repeats only is acceptable as a display next to the real gate.

candidate: Single-use final-test ledger: durable receipt before opening, hash-chained append-only records
what: The final test set is opened once; a receipt is written durably first; every ledger line carries the hash of the previous line.
problem_here: Held-out test must stay unread until final evaluation and the history must be tamper-evident.
mechanism: Receipt file written and flushed before evaluation starts; a second open is refused; chain check on every start.
evidence: arXiv 2611.06607 v1 (2026-11-04, single-author preprint, finance): holdout opened 'exactly once, after a durable receipt is written'; 'hash-chained, append-only ledger'; a survivor with Sharpe near 3 'fell to 0.26 on its single holdout use'. arXiv 1502.04585 (Blum and Hardt): repeated submissions 'may begin to overfit to the holdout data'.
maturity: Simple mechanism; the supporting paper is a preprint from another domain.
cost: A few dozen lines of stdlib code.
simpler_alternative: A flag file that marks the test set as used.
reason: Serves the first-ranked quality attribute directly and costs nothing at run time. Agrees with the loop-autoresearch scout.
cheap_local_trial: Unit test: a second open attempt is refused and editing one ledger line breaks the chain check.

candidate: Config-only loop mode: proposals as declarative JSON over a declared vocabulary
what: In this mode the agent may only emit a JSON proposal over declared hyperparameters; trusted harness code validates, runs and decides.
problem_here: Agent-written code would otherwise need sandboxing and review in unattended mode.
mechanism: Schema check of the proposal; unknown keys refused; no file edits by the agent.
evidence: arXiv 2611.06607 v1: the model 'proposes, and only trusted code decides'; proposals are 'strict declarative JSON over a fixed vocabulary, so there is no model-written code to sandbox'.
maturity: One preprint; the idea is simple.
cost: Small; limits what the loop can discover.
simpler_alternative: Code-editing loop with the guard hook.
reason: Removes a whole risk class for hyperparameter-only loops; whether agents still find gains under the restriction is untested here.
cheap_local_trial: Ten iterations on the bundled task with JSON-only proposals against ten with code edits, same gate and budget.

candidate: Duplicate-configuration refusal by content hash before a run is spent
what: Hash the change plus configuration; refuse a launch whose hash was already scored.
problem_here: Run budget is the scarce resource of the loop.
mechanism: sha256 lookup in the ledger before launch.
evidence: arXiv 2611.06607 v1: duplicates refused 'before they spend a trial'; autoresearch-mlx rigor.py skips configurations already scored by hash.
simpler_alternative: Let the agent remember what it tried.
reason: Exact duplicates are a pure waste and the check cannot harm validity. The loop-autoresearch scout rates it Trial because near-duplicates are not caught.
cheap_local_trial: Submit the same change twice on the bundled task; the second launch must be refused.

candidate: Harness-owned timer, evaluation call and seed (none of them inside agent-editable files)
what: Wall-clock budget, the call of the evaluator and the seed are set and measured by harness code outside the files the agent may edit.
problem_here: The evaluator must not be changeable by the agent.
mechanism: Evaluation in a separate process from a protected file; budget enforced by the run controller; seed passed in by the harness.
evidence: karpathy/autoresearch @228791fb program.md: prepare.py is read-only by instruction only; the editable train.py holds the budget check and calls evaluate_bpb (seen in the andyluo7 fork: 'if step > 10 and total_training_time >= TIME_BUDGET'). The 'immutable evaluator' of the Gemini report is therefore contradicted.
simpler_alternative: An instruction not to edit prepare.py, as upstream does.
reason: Upstream leaves all three within reach of the agent; the brief forbids that. Agrees with the loop-autoresearch scout.
cheap_local_trial: Tamper fixture: a change that edits the budget constant or skips evaluation must not change the harness-measured result, or must be marked invalid.
checked: github.com/karpathy/autoresearch README and program.md @228791fb; andyluo7/autoresearch train.py; 2026-11-11

candidate: Checks gate before keep (correctness checks run by the harness after every successful run)
what: A protected checks command runs after each run that exits 0; a failure gives the state checks_failed and the keep is refused.
problem_here: A better metric from a broken or invalid run must not be kept.
mechanism: Own timeout (pi default 300 s); checks time excluded from the metric.
evidence: pi-autoresearch v1.9.0 README: .auto/checks.sh 'runs automatically after every benchmark that exits 0'; keep refused on failure; 'Checks execution time does not affect the primary metric.'
maturity: Shipped feature of a tool with 8,230 stars.
reason: Cheap deterministic backstop; in the kit the checks file must be protected, unlike pi where the agent writes it.
cheap_local_trial: Add a check that fails on NaN loss to the bundled task and feed it a run that diverges.

candidate: Loop state in files so that a fresh or compacted session resumes deterministically
what: Goal, append-only log and idea list live in harness-owned files; after compaction or restart the agent is told to re-read them.
problem_here: Unattended runs outlive one context window.
mechanism: Fixed resume prompt that names the files; no reliance on chat memory.
evidence: pi-autoresearch v1.9.0: deterministic summary on compaction, then the agent is re-prompted to re-read .auto/prompt.md, the log tail, ideas and git log.
simpler_alternative: Trust the compaction summary of the agent.
reason: Makes long loops restartable on every agent product. Agrees with the scouts that propose one fresh session per iteration.
cheap_local_trial: Kill the agent mid-loop on the bundled task and restart; the next iteration must continue from the log.

candidate: Hard iteration cap and consecutive-failure stop in the loop controller
what: The controller stops at a maximum number of iterations and after a set number of failures in a row.
problem_here: Unattended mode must be bounded by user limits.
mechanism: Counters in harness state; checked before each launch.
evidence: pi-autoresearch v1.9.0 code: AUTORESUME_TURN_LIMIT = 200, CONSECUTIVE_FAILURE_OVERRIDE_LIMIT = 20, maxIterations in .auto/config.json; the Ruby port defaults maxIterations to 50. Upstream program.md instead says 'LOOP FOREVER' and 'NEVER STOP'.
reason: Required by the brief; the community ports added caps after upstream shipped none.
cheap_local_trial: Set the cap to 2 on the bundled task and confirm the third launch is refused.
checked: pi-autoresearch index.ts v1.9.0; marcelopazzo/claude-code-autoresearch README; karpathy/autoresearch program.md; 2026-11-11

candidate: Outer supervisor process as loop driver (one agent process per iteration)
what: A stdlib controller starts the agent for one iteration, waits, measures, decides and starts the next.
problem_here: Nobody answers prompts and the agent must not decide when the loop ends.
mechanism: Subprocess per iteration; state in files.
evidence: Claude Code hooks page: Stop-hook continuation has an '8-consecutive-continuation cap'; Codex /goal completion is declared by the working model itself (openai/codex ref c9bbed2d). Both in-session drivers leave control with the agent.
maturity: Pattern used by several community loops.
reason: Only driver that keeps limits and decisions outside the agent on all three products. Agrees with the platform scouts.
cheap_local_trial: Two iterations on the bundled task with a stub agent command.

candidate: Stop-hook loop driver (marcelopazzo/claude-code-autoresearch and the Gemini report)
what: A Stop hook answers with decision 'block' so the session keeps going.
problem_here: Proposed as the Claude Code loop engine.
mechanism: Exit code 2 or decision block on Stop.
evidence: Claude Code hooks page: exit code 2 on Stop 'Prevents Claude from stopping'; but 'after stop hooks have continued the turn eight times in a row, Claude Code overrides the next block and ends the turn' (count resets on a tool call; CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP raises it).
reason: The agent session stays in charge of the loop and context grows without bound; the report did not mention the cap.

candidate: AGENTS.md as single rules file plus a CLAUDE.md that only contains @AGENTS.md (no symbolic link)
what: One rules file for all agents; Claude Code gets it through a one-line import.
problem_here: Three agent products must read the same rules, also on native Windows.
mechanism: Import line; no link; each file short.
evidence: Claude Code memory page: AGENTS.md is read natively from v2.1.277 only when no CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md exists; the import 'never makes Claude read AGENTS.md twice'; on Windows 'use the @AGENTS.md import instead' of a symlink; 'target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file'.
reason: Works on every version and OS; the claim of the ChatGPT report is verified. Agrees with the agent-standards scout.
cheap_local_trial: Install into an empty folder and ask each agent to quote one rule.

candidate: Claude Code OS sandbox with filesystem denyRead for sealed data (WSL2, Linux, macOS)
what: Enable the sandbox and list the sealed test folder under sandbox.filesystem.denyRead; switch off the unsandboxed escape hatch.
problem_here: Read deny rules alone do not stop a Python script from opening the test set.
mechanism: OS-level block for all Bash subprocesses.
evidence: Permissions page: Read deny rules 'don't apply ... to arbitrary subprocesses ... like a Python or Node script that opens files itself. For OS-level enforcement ... enable the sandbox.' Sandboxing page: 'The sandbox is off by default.'; 'On native Windows, Claude Code runs commands unsandboxed.' Contradicts the Gemini report.
cost: Setup per machine; GPU access inside the sandbox untested.
simpler_alternative: Guard hook plus keeping sealed data outside the project.
reason: Only real enforcement available on Claude Code; missing test is whether GPU training runs inside it. Agrees with the platform-claude-code scout.
cheap_local_trial: On WSL2: enable the sandbox with denyRead on a dummy folder; a one-line Python read must fail while a short GPU run still works.

candidate: Enforcement matrix in the docs: per agent and OS, what is enforced and what is advice
what: One table that says for each protection whether a hook, a sandbox or only an instruction stands behind it.
problem_here: The brief requires docs to state enforced versus advice.
mechanism: Table generated from the self-test results of the installer.
evidence: Claude Code: sandbox off by default and absent on native Windows; Codex subagents page: 'Custom agent instructions can ask an agent to avoid edits, but they don't create a separate read-only sandbox.' The Gemini report presents both as enforced.
reason: The reports show how easily advice is mistaken for enforcement.

candidate: Unattended Claude Code launcher: never --bare, explicit permission mode, guard-hook canary first
what: claude -p with an explicit permission mode and allowlist, --permission-prompts none, JSON output; the first step proves the guard hook denies a forbidden call.
problem_here: A run whose guard hook silently did not load is unprotected.
mechanism: Launcher flags plus a canary denial check before any training.
evidence: Headless page: hooks do not run in bare mode and --bare 'will become the default for -p in a future release'; from v2.1.302 'claude -p runs start in Manual mode when nothing sets a permission mode'; without --bare a -p session runs project hooks and connects .mcp.json servers 'even in a folder you've never trusted'.
reason: Defaults are changing under the kit; the canary makes a silent loss of the guard visible. Agrees with the platform-claude-code scout.
cheap_local_trial: Start a one-turn headless session in a test folder and check that the canary call is denied by the hook.

candidate: Detached training runs (not children of the agent shell)
what: The run controller starts training as a detached process.
problem_here: Stopping or timing out the agent must not kill a live run.
evidence: Headless page: 'On SIGTERM, Claude Code terminates the process tree of any Bash command that is still running'.
reason: Keep the existing design; the vendor behaviour confirms why.
cheap_local_trial: Launch a run, terminate the agent process, check the run continues.

candidate: Agent-token and cost metering from machine-readable agent output
what: The supervisor reads token usage from codex exec --json turn.completed events and total_cost_usd from claude -p JSON output and charges them to the budget ledger.
problem_here: User limits include agent tokens and money.
mechanism: Parse JSON lines; stop when the limit is reached.
evidence: Codex non-interactive page: --json events include token usage in turn.completed and no flags for turn, time or token limits are documented; Claude Code headless page: --output-format json includes total_cost_usd and --max-budget-usd exists.
reason: Only way to enforce a token limit on Codex, which documents none of its own.
cheap_local_trial: Run one short headless turn per agent and print the parsed usage.

candidate: Codex unattended invocation: codex exec --sandbox workspace-write --ephemeral --json with overrides, no [profiles.*] table
what: The launcher passes sandbox and approval settings on the command line or through a separate profile file.
problem_here: Codex port of the unattended loop.
evidence: Non-interactive page: 'By default, codex exec runs in a read-only sandbox.'; '--full-auto is no longer supported.' Config docs: 'In Codex 0.134.0 and later, --profile no longer reads [profiles.profile-name] from config.toml'. The [profiles.autoresearch] table of the Gemini report is contradicted.
maturity: Documented; Codex CLI 0.167.0 per the platform-codex scout.
reason: Verified flags; avoids writing to user-level config. Agrees with the platform-codex scout.
cheap_local_trial: codex exec with a trivial prompt in a test folder; confirm sandbox mode and usage events in the JSON stream.

candidate: Codex custom agents (.codex/agents/*.toml) for reviewer and analyst, documented as advice-only read-only
what: TOML files with name, description and developer_instructions define the two helper agents.
problem_here: Port of the read-only reviewer subagents.
mechanism: Agent files; read-only enforced only if the guard hook does it.
evidence: Codex subagents page: 'sandbox_mode, approval_policy, model_provider, and mcp_servers, don't override the parent configuration'; 'they don't create a separate read-only sandbox'. The sandbox_mode = 'read-only' line in an agent file of the Gemini report is contradicted.
simpler_alternative: A separate codex exec --sandbox read-only process for reviews.
reason: The files work; the read-only property must come from the hook or a separate process and the docs must say so. Agrees with the platform-codex scout.
cheap_local_trial: Ask the Codex reviewer agent to write a file in a test folder and see whether anything stops it.

candidate: Codex /goal as driver of the unattended loop
what: Persistent objective with automatic continuation.
problem_here: Proposed as the Codex loop engine.
mechanism: The working model calls the update_goal tool to mark the goal complete or blocked.
evidence: openai/codex main (ref c9bbed2d), codex-rs/ext/goal: 'Set status to complete only when the objective has actually been achieved and no required work remains.' No separate evaluator model exists in the source; the claim of the Gemini report is contradicted. Behaviour under codex exec: not checked (accepted as given by the user).
reason: Completion is self-declared by the agent, which the brief rules out for keep and stop decisions.

candidate: Throughput profiling step before any search under a fixed wall-clock budget
what: Before the loop: measure data-loading share, steps per second and GPU use; fix obvious bottlenecks; then freeze the setup as baseline.
problem_here: Under a wall-clock budget, speed changes look like model improvements.
mechanism: Step-timing split in the run logger; one profiling run.
evidence: Google tuning playbook: 'Use an appropriate profiler to diagnose input-bound pipelines.'; autoresearch-mlx README: 'smaller faster-training models can beat larger ones simply by fitting more optimizer steps into the budget'; Hernandez blog (one machine, single runs): compile settings moved val_bpb 1.090 to 1.053 at 15 minutes. No controlled study found.
maturity: Common practice; quantitative evidence is anecdotal.
simpler_alternative: Let the loop discover speed-ups itself.
reason: Costs one run and separates speed effects from modelling effects; speed changes still need a numerics check.
cheap_local_trial: Profile the bundled task once and report the data-loading share of step time.
checked: tuning_playbook README; autoresearch-mlx README; hectorhernandez.dev post; 2026-11-11

candidate: Rule: kept settings are tied to budget and hardware; re-baseline when either changes
what: A change of time budget, GPU type or batch size invalidates the baseline and the noise floor.
problem_here: Results from one setup are otherwise carried to another as if they held.
mechanism: Baseline record stores budget and hardware; mismatch forces new baseline repeats.
evidence: Hernandez blog: best depth 5 at 5 minutes but 7 at 15 minutes (single account); autoresearch-mlx README: findings from one machine 'did not carry cleanly' to another; tuning playbook: 'The optimal values of most hyperparameters are sensitive to the batch size.' The loop-autoresearch scout cites arXiv 2610.10491 for the same point (not re-read here).
maturity: Consistent across sources of mixed quality.
cost: Extra baseline runs after a change.
reason: Directly protects validity of comparisons and matters for the remote-GPU module.
checked: hectorhernandez.dev post; autoresearch-mlx README; tuning_playbook README; 2026-11-11

candidate: Rule text: split before any preprocessing; group or entity split when samples are dependent
what: Reference text plus a check that asks for the group key before a split is accepted.
problem_here: Leakage through preprocessing or shared entities inflates validation scores.
mechanism: Checklist item; the data scout proposes a stdlib hash-bucket group split.
evidence: scikit-learn 1.9.1 docs: 'Always split the data into train and test subsets first, particularly before any preprocessing steps.'; GroupKFold 'ensures that the same group is not represented in both testing and training sets'; the leaky feature-selection example scores 0.76 against 0.5.
reason: The claims of the ChatGPT report are verified against the official docs.
checked: scikit-learn.org 1.9.1 common pitfalls and cross-validation pages; 2026-11-11

candidate: Guard rules for publishing and paid-job actions (push_to_hub, hf jobs, hf_jobs tool, tracker delete)
what: In unattended mode the guard denies Hub pushes, job submissions and tracker deletions unless the user enabled the matching module.
problem_here: Vendor skills publish models or spend money by default.
mechanism: Pattern rules in the existing guard hook.

simpler_alternative: Telling users not to install those skills.

candidate: Finalize: split kept changes into independent branches from the merge-base
what: After a loop, kept experiments are grouped and each group becomes its own branch for review.
problem_here: A long loop leaves one tangled history.
mechanism: Groups must not share files; branches cut from the merge-base.
evidence: pi-autoresearch v1.9.0 README: '/autoresearch finalize' groups kept experiments and 'creates independent branches from the merge-base'.
simpler_alternative: One summary diff plus the journal.
reason: Helps human review; value for training code, where changes interact, is untested.
cheap_local_trial: After ten iterations on the bundled task, split the kept commits by hand and check each applies alone.

candidate: Revert rule: the harness reverts in its own branch or worktree, never git reset --hard or git clean on the user tree
what: Discarded changes are dropped by checking out the last kept commit of a loop branch.
problem_here: Destructive git commands can delete untracked results or user work.
mechanism: Dedicated loop branch; untracked run data kept outside it.
evidence: marcelopazzo/claude-code-autoresearch README: on discard it will 'reset HEAD to the pre-run commit and clean the working tree'; the contract in the Gemini report uses git reset --hard HEAD~1; upstream keeps results.tsv untracked.
simpler_alternative: git reset --hard as in the reports.
reason: Prevents data loss in unattended mode.
cheap_local_trial: Create an untracked file, discard an iteration, check the file survives.

candidate: Claude Code subagent frontmatter isolation: worktree for loop workers
what: A subagent runs in its own git worktree.
problem_here: Isolation of candidate edits.
evidence: Sub-agents page: field verified; hooks from settings 'apply inside subagents'; unrecognised frontmatter fields are ignored silently.
cost: Guard paths must resolve inside the worktree.
simpler_alternative: One fresh process per iteration in the main tree.
reason: Verified to exist; untested whether sealed-path and run-protection rules still match inside a worktree.
cheap_local_trial: Start a worktree subagent in a test repository and have it try to read a path the guard denies.

candidate: Hernandez ROCm autoresearch write-up (the '316-run study') as a list of hypotheses
what: Personal blog post of 2026-04-10 on about 316 single-run experiments on one AMD GPU.

mechanism: Sessions of 231, 25 and 15 experiments; final val_bpb 1.0446.
evidence: Blog read: default compile 1.090 to 1.077 and mode max-autotune to 1.053 at a 15-minute budget, MFU 13.3% to 19.0% (report says 20.0%); '+43%' steps is relative to default compile; 25 regularisation trials gave 0 keeps; cross-seed variance about 0.005 val_bpb; no seed repeats before keeping.
simpler_alternative: The dated technique cards of the kit.
reason: Usable as hypotheses for the loop, not as rules: a single blog is Unverified by the standard of the brief.

what: Solution-tree search agent for ML tasks.

checked: GitHub API and README; arxiv.org/abs/2410.07095 v6; 2026-11-11

candidate: Branching search as an optional strategy under the same harness gate (idea from AIDE and OpenEvolve)
what: From the current best, try several independent candidates and keep the best that passes the gate.
problem_here: Linear loops can stall on one line of ideas.
mechanism: Controller schedules b candidates per round from the same parent.
evidence: MLE-bench Table 2 shows a tree-search scaffold at about twice the medal rate of a linear agent at equal model, on Kaggle tasks; no result for short training loops. The Gemini rule 'switch after 15 discards' has no source (issue #22 does not contain it).
cost: b times the runs per round.
reason: Plausible, but the test at equal run budget is missing.
cheap_local_trial: Same run budget on the bundled task: linear against best-of-three branching, three campaigns each.

what: New clustering algorithm in FAISS.
problem_here: Named in both reports.
mechanism: faiss.contrib.e_means: Emeans (needs PyTorch) and NumpyEmeans (faiss and NumPy only).
evidence: arXiv 2611.09501 v1 (6 Nov 2026); FAISS v1.16.0 (10 Nov 2026), MIT. Tried 2026-11-12, faiss-cpu 1.16.0, native Windows, 200,000 points, three synthetic sets, 3 seeds: `NumpyEmeans` (5 passes) ended 0.1 to 3.9 % below the error of `faiss.Kmeans` (25 passes) in 0.42 to 0.58 of the time. Within 0.1 % of 100 Lloyd passes or better; with 2.5 passes 3.6 % below on clustered data and 0.2 % above on the other two sets, in a fifth of the time. The authors' 10 to 45 times is for GPUs and was not tried. Not tried on real embeddings; no independent replication.
maturity: A week old: paper of 6 Nov 2026, release of 10 Nov 2026.
reason: Clustering has one place in the kit: grouping embeddings of a corpus too large for exact comparison (near-duplicates inside clusters, a subset balanced over clusters, errors by cluster). There e-means replaces k-means: on a CPU here it matched or beat 25 Lloyd passes in about half the time.
